record.context_brief: Singular reductions of NLS and compressible Euler
record.original_question: Can one derive a direct reduction from the three-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation to the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation through singular solutions, without passing through the localized induction approximation? Similarly, can compressible Euler equations be reduced from three dimensions to singular solutions supported on one-dimensional submanifolds?

artifact.category_tag: Singular reductions of NLS and Euler
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation in three spatial dimensions,
\[
 i\,\partial_t \psi + \Delta \psi + |\psi|^2\psi = 0,\qquad \psi:\mathbb{R}_t\times\mathbb{R}^3_x\to\mathbb{C},
\]
and, separately, the compressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$,
\[
 \partial_t \rho + \nabla\!\cdot(\rho u)=0,\qquad \partial_t(\rho u) + \nabla\!\cdot(\rho u\otimes u) + \nabla p(\rho)=0,
\]
for density $\rho:\mathbb{R}_t\times\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$, velocity $u:\mathbb{R}_t\times\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}^3$, and a prescribed equation of state $p=p(\rho)$.

It is classically known that the localized induction (binormal-flow) approximation for a vortex filament $\gamma(t,s)\subset\mathbb{R}^3$, $\gamma_t=\gamma_s\times\gamma_{ss}$, can be mapped via the Hasimoto transform to the one-dimensional cubic NLS
\[
 i\,\partial_t q + \partial_s^2 q + \tfrac{1}{2}|q|^2 q = 0.
\]
The questions are the following.

(a) Construct a direct reduction of the three-dimensional cubic NLS to the one-dimensional cubic NLS by considering a class of solutions $\psi$ that are singular and concentrated on a moving one-dimensional submanifold (curve) $\gamma(t,\cdot)\subset\mathbb{R}^3$, such that the resulting effective dynamics for an associated complex amplitude along the curve is governed by the 1D cubic NLS — without invoking the localized induction approximation as an intermediate step.

(b) Analogously, construct a reduction of the three-dimensional compressible Euler system to a self-consistent dynamics for singular solutions whose support lies on a one-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^3$, deriving the equations of motion for such curve-supported singular Euler solutions.

Determine whether such direct reductions exist, and if so describe the admissible ansätze and the resulting one-dimensional evolution equations.
artifact.status_search_result: No published direct reduction of 3D NLS to 1D NLS through curve-supported singular solutions (bypassing the localized induction approximation) was found; existing links pass through the binormal/Hasimoto route or rely on symmetry reductions. Likewise, no curve-supported singular reduction of 3D compressible Euler was located. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Localized induction equation, Heisenberg chain, and nonlinear Schrodinger equation
status_evidence.snippet: Hasimoto transform relates the binormal flow / localized induction equation to the 1D cubic NLS.
status_evidence.claim: Existing link from filament dynamics to 1D NLS goes through the localized induction approximation, not directly from 3D NLS.

status_evidence.title: Class of Solutions to the 3D Cubic Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation that Blows Up on a Circle
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs 3D NLS solutions concentrating (blowing up) on a one-dimensional curve, but does not derive a 1D NLS reduction along the curve.
status_evidence.claim: Singular curve-concentrated 3D NLS solutions exist, but a direct effective 1D NLS reduction on the curve is not established.

status_evidence.title: The Hasimoto Transformation for a Finite Length Vortex Filament
status_evidence.snippet: Hasimoto transformation maps filament dynamics under LIA to 1D NLS.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reductions still proceed through LIA.
